classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 in `stsz_box_read`; semantically the fault is an out-of-bounds read from the heap-allocated compact sample-size array `ptr->sizes`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42494345 (gpac): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target fuzz_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42494345
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta / OSS-Fuzz report / staged vulnerable source / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The staged 74-byte witness is a single root-level `stz2` box. In `gf_isom_box_parse_ex`, bytes `00 00 00 00 73 74 7a 32` become `size = 0` and `type = stz2`; because the box is at root, the size-0 special case converts that into a full box extent of 74 bytes. The generic parser then stores `newBox->size = 74 - 8 = 66`, `gf_isom_full_box_read` consumes the 4-byte full-box header and leaves 62, and `stsz_box_read` consumes the compact-table header and leaves `ptr->size == 54` while materializing field-size byte `0` and `sampleCount == 107`. The repair heuristic sees `estSize = 54 / 107 == 0` and `(107 + 1) / 2 == 54`, so it forces `ptr->sampleSize = 4`. The 4-bit guard still passes because `107 / 2 == 53` and `53 > 54` is false, so `ptr->sizes` is allocated for 107 `u32` entries. On the final odd-sample iteration the 4-bit arm writes only `sizes[106]`, consumes one padding nibble, and advances `i` from 106 to 108. The shared post-switch accounting statement `if (ptr->max_size < ptr->sizes[i])` then reuses that post-incremented index and reads 4 bytes past the 428-byte heap allocation. The fix introduces `s_size` and moves `max_size`, `total_size`, and `total_samples` updates into each switch arm before `i` is advanced.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes the witness and materializes the root box's size/type state. On this path it creates both the `stz2` dispatch key and the root-size-to-EOF extent that later becomes `ptr->size` inside `stsz_box_read`.
source.value_from: The staged witness `poc` is 74 bytes (sha256 `620c028e1eaa4ab1892f7f4d4fc67aac2688c02cbbe7241377750519bff59e6b`). Bytes 0-3 are `00 00 00 00`, so line 113 reads `size == 0`. Bytes 4-7 are `73 74 7a 32`, so line 120 reads `type == 'stz2'`. Because parsing starts at a root box, lines 125-130 convert that zero size into `gf_bs_available(bs) + 8 == 66 + 8 == 74`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The shared post-switch accounting reuses the loop index after the 4-bit arm has already advanced it, so the final odd iteration dereferences `ptr->sizes[108]` instead of the last written `ptr->sizes[106]`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by introducing `s_size` and updating `max_size`, `total_size`, and `total_samples` inside each switch arm before `i` is incremented.

sink.description: Crash site. The first out-of-bounds read occurs when the shared accounting epilogue evaluates `ptr->sizes[i]` with `i == 108` against a 107-element heap allocation.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` at `stsz_box_read` line 5667, on address `0x6140000001f0`, which is 4 bytes to the right of the 428-byte `ptr->sizes` region allocated at line 5646.

tainted_value_origin.description: After the earlier root-header and full-box reductions, the compact-table header bytes become the vulnerability-relevant payload values `i == 0` and `sampleCount == 107`, while the remaining box size is reduced to 54 bytes.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Witness bytes 12-19 are `02 0e 02 00 00 00 00 6b`. The first three are consumed as the reserved field, the fourth becomes the explicit field-size byte `0`, and the last four become `sampleCount == 107`.

e = gf_isom_full_box_read(newBox, bs);
if (!e) e = gf_isom_box_read(newBox, bs);
parser_admitted.description: After the root header is materialized and reduced to a payload size, the generic parser dispatches the root `stz2` box into its registered reader `stsz_box_read`.

fine_trace.note: Source. Root header bytes `00 00 00 00 73 74 7a 32` are consumed here as `size == 0` and `type == GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_STZ2`. Because the box is at root, the size-0 special case converts that header into an actual box extent of 74 bytes, which is the size state later reduced inside the vulnerable reader.

The root-box extent from step 1 is converted into per-box payload state. With `size == 74` and `hdr_size == 8`, the new `stz2` box enters the reader path with `newBox->size == 66` bytes remaining after the outer header.
Because `stz2` is a full box, the generic full-box reader consumes bytes 8-11 as version and flags before the box-specific body. This decrements the carried payload remainder from 66 to 62.

The compact-table header is consumed here. `ISOM_DECREASE_SIZE(ptr, 8)` reduces the remaining payload from 62 to 54, the reserved bytes `02 0e 02` are skipped, the explicit field-size byte becomes `i == 0`, and the next four bytes become `ptr->sampleCount == 107`.

Because step 4 produced `i == 0`, the parser takes the `default` repair path instead of the literal 4/8/16-bit cases. With `ptr->size == 54` and `sampleCount == 107`, `estSize` is 0 and `(107 + 1) / 2 == 54`, so the heuristic forces `ptr->sampleSize = 4`.

Present guard. On the inferred 4-bit path, the reader rejects only when `ptr->sampleCount / 2 > ptr->size`. Here integer division yields `107 / 2 == 53`, so `53 > 54` is false and parsing continues into allocation and iteration.

The accepted `sampleCount` sizes the destination array. This allocates `107 * sizeof(u32) == 428` bytes and sets `alloc_size` to 107, so valid indices are `0..106`. The saved ASan allocation stack points back to this statement.

Earlier paired iterations are collapsed because they only repeat the same two-entry store. By the final loop entry, `i == 106`. The 4-bit arm stores the last real sample into `sizes[106]`; because `i + 1 < ptr->sampleCount` is false for the odd tail, it consumes one padding nibble instead of writing `sizes[107]`, then advances `i` to 108. The highest initialized slot remains 106.

Root cause and sink. The shared accounting epilogue reuses `i` after step 8 has already advanced it to 108. Against the 107-element heap allocation from step 7, the first `ptr->sizes[i]` read accesses 4 bytes beyond the 428-byte region. Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports the crash at this exact statement, and the patch fixes it by doing per-entry accounting inside each switch arm before `i` changes.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42494345 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged 74-byte `poc` to `/out/fuzz_parse` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `stsz_box_read`.

format.name: raw root-level ISO BMFF `stz2` box
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 74-byte witness staged in `poc`: `00 00 00 00 73 74 7a 32 01 ce 64 61 02 0e 02 00 00 00 00 6b 7a 00 42 73 64 73 25 0e 0d f0 02 0e 02 00 00 00 00 80 00 43 00 11 01 00 04 00 00 67 00 00 80 00 6b 7a 11 01 00 04 00 00 67 00 00 80 00 4b 61 3e 61 3e 00 65 73 68`. Bytes 0-3 make it a root box with size 0, so GPAC reads the box to EOF as a 74-byte root `stz2` box. The parser then carries `newBox->size = 66`, `gf_isom_full_box_read` reduces that to 62, and the compact-header read reduces it to 54 while producing field-size byte `0` and `sampleCount == 107`. Because the repair heuristic sees `(107 + 1) / 2 == 54`, it infers `sampleSize = 4`. The final odd-sample iteration therefore writes only `sizes[106]`, consumes one padding nibble, advances `i` to 108, and the shared `ptr->sizes[i]` accounting read overflows the 107-entry array. This contract is grounded only for this exact witness layout and the same reconstructed `stz2` size/count state; Stage 02 does not establish a broader input class beyond reproducing that same path.
